sentence_stem: If only I had listened to my advice,
correct_completion: I would not have made that mistake.
full_sentence: If only I had listened to my advice, I would not have made that mistake.
acceptable_variants: I wouldn't have made that mistake.
I would have avoided this problem.

options.text: I will make that mistake again.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' points to the future. 'If only' with a past form expresses regret about the past, so a past conditional is needed.

options.text: I don't make mistakes like that.
options.why_wrong: This is a present general statement. It does not express regret about a past action.

options.text: I would not have made that mistake.

options.why_wrong: This reports a real past event. It does not express an unreal wish or regret.

grammar_focus: Wishes about the past with 'if only' plus past perfect and 'would have'
explanation: After 'if only', the past perfect expresses a wish about something that did not happen. The main clause then uses 'would have' plus a past participle to show the imagined result. Learners often use a simple past or a present form here because the regret concerns the past, so the past perfect and 'would have' are required. Turkish speakers may also be tempted to use a simple past in the main clause, because they map the regret directly onto one past tense.
translation: Keşke tavsiyeme kulak verseydim, o hatayı yapmazdım.
